In 2012, a group of Indigenous NRL players including Dean Widders, Preston Campbell, Timana Tahu and George Rose came together to develop a pre-game ceremony that would be a response to New Zealand’s much loved, universally recognised and hugely respected haka. Rather than simply taking an existing dance, the players came up with a series of movements that reflected cultural symbols - the clan, the warrior, the boomerang, the spear. programme.desc: Go Karts is a thrilling family film about a boy who must overcome tremendous odds and his own recklessness to achieve his dream of winning the National Go Kart Championship.

programme.title: Argo
programme.desc: Ben Affleck directs and stars in this real-life political intelligence dramedy based on a true story. Acting under the cover of a Hollywood producer scouting a location for a science fiction film, a CIA agent launches a dangerous operation to rescue six Americans in Tehran during the U.S. hostage crisis in Iran in 1979.

programme.title: Baghdad Messi
programme.desc: After losing a leg in a devastating attack, 11-year-old Hamoudi refuses to give up on his dream of becoming a football star like Lionel Messi. An inspiring story of courage, hope and determination.

programme.title: Music And Lyrics
programme.desc: A washed-up pop star teams up with an aspiring writer to compose a hit song for a teen idol, discovering love and second chances through music in this charming 2007 romantic comedy.

programme.title: Bonjour Anne: Paris Can Wait
programme.desc: Eleanor Coppola’s narrative directorial and screenwriting debut stars Academy Award nominee Diane Lane as a Hollywood producer’s wife who unexpectedly takes a trip through France, which reawakens her sense of self and her joie de vivre. Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.title: The Silver Brumby
programme.desc: During a violent storm in the Victorian Highlands, a mother tells her frightened daughter a fable about a great silver brumby who must find its place among its kind, while one man, living in the wilderness, is determined to capture the brumby and tame it. Directed by John Tatoulis and stars Russell Crowe and Caroline Goodall.

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.desc: Centrering her fearless approach to storytelling and her commitment to truth telling through Blak perspectives. Leah sits down with Rachel Perkins to trace a powerful career across stage and screen.

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.sub-title: Erica Glynn - My Bed, Your Bed
programme.desc: In this episode Erica Glynn reflects on a career grounded in storytelling, mentorship and cultural authority. Anchored by her short film My Bed, Your Bed.

programme.title: Unmoored
programme.desc: Maria is a successful Swedish TV presenter whose life is turned upside down by shocking accusations made against her husband. To avoid the media attention, they head south on sabbatical. However, an unexpected confrontation triggers a desperate chain of events. Alone, Maria flees to the solitude of the English moors, but her new idyll soon turns to paranoia. As her guilt grows, she is forced to examine the depths of her own self-deception in this psychological suspense drama.

programme.title: Yolngu Boy
programme.desc: About the coming-of-age of three Aboriginal boys in Arnhem Land who inhabit two cultures at once - that of North-East Arnhem Land and also western culture. Botj, Lorrpu and Milika are three Yolngu teenagers who once shared a dream of becoming great hunters. Now aged 14, only Lorrpu hasn't diverged. Botj is a lost soul in trouble with the law, and Milika is more interested in football and girls. One of the central themes of the film is the divide between the prosperity-driven, materialistic western ideal of life and the everyday reality faced by young Aborigines. Directed by Stephen Johnson, and stars Sean Mununggurr and John Sebastian Pilakui.

programme.desc: An intimate portrait of a man driven to share his culture with the world. In 2012, a group of Indigenous NRL players including Dean Widders, Preston Campbell, Timana Tahu and George Rose came together to develop a pre-game ceremony that would be a response to New Zealand’s much loved, universally recognised and hugely respected haka. Rather than simply taking an existing dance, the players came up with a series of movements that reflected cultural symbols - the clan, the warrior, the boomerang, the spear. They concluded their new dance with a moment of reflection - to them, this emphasised that the silences are just as important, or even more important, than the spoken words.

programme.desc: Told in one fluid real-time shot, this film follows a 19th century French aristocrat - notorious for his scathing memoirs about life in Russia - as he travels through the majestic spaces of the Hermitage in St. Petersburg, engaging real and imagined characters from Russian and European history. The Hermitage - home to generations of Romonovs and the repository of so much Russian history - is the ark of the Russian soul, which he guards affectionately until the world sees better days. Directed by Aleksandr Sokurov, and stars Mariya Kuznetsova and Sergei Dontsov. (From Russia, in Russian, English subtitles) (Drama) (2002) (Rpt) G WS

Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

Directed by John Tatoulis and stars Russell Crowe and Caroline Goodall.

programme.title: Frame By Frame

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.sub-title: Erica Glynn - My Bed, Your Bed
programme.desc: In this episode Erica Glynn reflects on a career grounded in storytelling, mentorship and cultural authority. Anchored by her short film My Bed, Your Bed.

programme.title: Unmoored
programme.desc: Maria is a successful Swedish TV presenter whose life is turned upside down by shocking accusations made against her husband. To avoid the media attention, they head south on sabbatical. However, an unexpected confrontation triggers a desperate chain of events. Alone, Maria flees to the solitude of the English moors, but her new idyll soon turns to paranoia. As her guilt grows, she is forced to examine the depths of her own self-deception in this psychological suspense drama.

programme.title: Yolngu Boy
programme.desc: About the coming-of-age of three Aboriginal boys in Arnhem Land who inhabit two cultures at once - that of North-East Arnhem Land and also western culture. Botj, Lorrpu and Milika are three Yolngu teenagers who once shared a dream of becoming great hunters. Now aged 14, only Lorrpu hasn't diverged. Botj is a lost soul in trouble with the law, and Milika is more interested in football and girls. One of the central themes of the film is the divide between the prosperity-driven, materialistic western ideal of life and the everyday reality faced by young Aborigines. Directed by Stephen Johnson, and stars Sean Mununggurr and John Sebastian Pilakui.

In 2012, a group of Indigenous NRL players including Dean Widders, Preston Campbell, Timana Tahu and George Rose came together to develop a pre-game ceremony that would be a response to New Zealand’s much loved, universally recognised and hugely respected haka. Rather than simply taking an existing dance, the players came up with a series of movements that reflected cultural symbols - the clan, the warrior, the boomerang, the spear. She gives her all to emulate her cool and successful cycle-pro father. But when the talented and ambitious young racer has to unwillingly swap saddles for a mountain bike things go haywire.

programme.title: Down With Love
programme.desc: When a ladies' man, man's man, man-about-town men's magazine journalist meets a popular pro-feminist author with a secret agenda of her own, a classic battle-of-the-sexes high jinx plot plays out to its expected happy "coupled" ending.

programme.title: The Idol

programme.title: The Way Ahead
programme.desc: A mismatched collection of conscripted civilians find training tough under Lieutenant Jim Perry and Sergeant Ned Fletcher when they are called up to replace an infantry battalion that had suffered casualties at Dunkirk.

programme.title: Time Bandits
programme.desc: Six fractious dwarfs steal a precious map that shows the locations of a series of time holes scattered across the universe, enabling them to travel back in time. Crashing through the bedroom wardrobe of 11 year old Craig Warnock and taking him along with them for the ride, they find themselves involved in a series of eccentric encounters with famous historical figures, amongst them Napoleon, Robin Hood and ancient Greece ruler, Agamemnon.

programme.title: Sanctuary
programme.desc: In a hotel room, Hal plans to end his dominatrix relationship with Rebecca before inheriting his father's fortune. But when she refuses to accept the rules of the game, their battle of power and control spirals.

He agrees to take part in a dangerous mission to save 123 Jewish orphans from the grasp of the Nazis and the ruthless Gestapo chief Klaus Barbie (Matthias Schweighöfer) and take them to safety across the border to Switzerland.

programme.title: I Accidentally Wrote A Book
programme.desc: The inspiring story of 12-year-old Nina, who discovers the healing power of writing. As she learns to write, Nina uncovers her family's history, experiences the long-suppressed grief of her long-lost mother, and gains a deeper sense of self.

programme.title: Lassie: A New Adventure
programme.desc: The most famous Collie dog Lassie is on a rescue mission with her best friend Flo and their new friends Henri, Kleo and little Pippa, a Jack Russell Terrier. This time round, Lassie's detective skills are particularly called upon to get to the bottom of the mysterious disappearances of several pedigree dogs.

programme.title: Dancing At Lughnasa
programme.desc: A young boy tells the story of growing up in a fatherless home with his unmarried mother and four spinster aunts in 1930s Ireland. (Meryl Streep, Catherine McCormack, Rhys Ifans)

programme.title: Russian Ark
programme.desc: Told in one fluid real-time shot, this film follows a 19th century French aristocrat - notorious for his scathing memoirs about life in Russia - as he travels through the majestic spaces of the Hermitage in St. Petersburg, engaging real and imagined characters from Russian and European history. Staged among some of Western Art's greatest masterpieces, climaxes in a pageant of colour, motion, and music. The Hermitage - home to generations of Romonovs and the repository of so much Russian history - is the ark of the Russian soul, which he guards affectionately until the world sees better days. Directed by Aleksandr Sokurov, and stars Mariya Kuznetsova and Sergei Dontsov. (From Russia, in Russian, English subtitles) (Drama) (2002) (Rpt) G WS

programme.title: Non-Stop
programme.desc: During a transatlantic flight from New York to London, veteran air marshal Bill Marks (Liam Neeson) receives anonymous messages threatening to kill a passenger every 20 minutes unless a ransom is paid. As panic spreads and suspicion turns towards him, Marks races to uncover the culprit before disaster strikes. Also stars Julianne Moore and Michelle Dockery.

programme.title: Argo
programme.desc: Ben Affleck directs and stars in this real-life political intelligence dramedy based on a true story. Acting under the cover of a Hollywood producer scouting a location for a science fiction film, a CIA agent launches a dangerous operation to rescue six Americans in Tehran during the U.S. hostage crisis in Iran in 1979.

programme.desc: Eleanor Coppola’s narrative directorial and screenwriting debut stars Academy Award nominee Diane Lane as a Hollywood producer’s wife who unexpectedly takes a trip through France, which reawakens her sense of self and her joie de vivre. Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.title: The Silver Brumby
programme.desc: During a violent storm in the Victorian Highlands, a mother tells her frightened daughter a fable about a great silver brumby who must find its place among its kind, while one man, living in the wilderness, is determined to capture the brumby and tame it. Directed by John Tatoulis and stars Russell Crowe and Caroline Goodall.

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.desc: Centrering her fearless approach to storytelling and her commitment to truth telling through Blak perspectives. Leah sits down with Rachel Perkins to trace a powerful career across stage and screen.

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.sub-title: Erica Glynn - My Bed, Your Bed
programme.desc: In this episode Erica Glynn reflects on a career grounded in storytelling, mentorship and cultural authority. Anchored by her short film My Bed, Your Bed.

programme.title: Unmoored
programme.desc: Maria is a successful Swedish TV presenter whose life is turned upside down by shocking accusations made against her husband. To avoid the media attention, they head south on sabbatical. However, an unexpected confrontation triggers a desperate chain of events. Alone, Maria flees to the solitude of the English moors, but her new idyll soon turns to paranoia. As her guilt grows, she is forced to examine the depths of her own self-deception in this psychological suspense drama.

programme.title: Yolngu Boy
programme.desc: About the coming-of-age of three Aboriginal boys in Arnhem Land who inhabit two cultures at once - that of North-East Arnhem Land and also western culture. Botj, Lorrpu and Milika are three Yolngu teenagers who once shared a dream of becoming great hunters. Now aged 14, only Lorrpu hasn't diverged. Botj is a lost soul in trouble with the law, and Milika is more interested in football and girls. One of the central themes of the film is the divide between the prosperity-driven, materialistic western ideal of life and the everyday reality faced by young Aborigines. Directed by Stephen Johnson, and stars Sean Mununggurr and John Sebastian Pilakui.

With survival suits on, and memories of the mast snapping fresh in their minds, the crew must confront the reality of their situation.

programme.title: Araatika! Rise Up
programme.desc: An intimate portrait of a man driven to share his culture with the world. In 2012, a group of Indigenous NRL players including Dean Widders, Preston Campbell, Timana Tahu and George Rose came together to develop a pre-game ceremony that would be a response to New Zealand’s much loved, universally recognised and hugely respected haka. Rather than simply taking an existing dance, the players came up with a series of movements that reflected cultural symbols - the clan, the warrior, the boomerang, the spear. They concluded their new dance with a moment of reflection - to them, this emphasised that the silences are just as important, or even more important, than the spoken words.

Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.desc: Maria is a successful Swedish TV presenter whose life is turned upside down by shocking accusations made against her husband. To avoid the media attention, they head south on sabbatical. However, an unexpected confrontation triggers a desperate chain of events. Alone, Maria flees to the solitude of the English moors, but her new idyll soon turns to paranoia. Botj, Lorrpu and Milika are three Yolngu teenagers who once shared a dream of becoming great hunters. Now aged 14, only Lorrpu hasn't diverged. Botj is a lost soul in trouble with the law, and Milika is more interested in football and girls. One of the central themes of the film is the divide between the prosperity-driven, materialistic western ideal of life and the everyday reality faced by young Aborigines. Directed by Stephen Johnson, and stars Sean Mununggurr and John Sebastian Pilakui.

programme.desc: An intimate portrait of a man driven to share his culture with the world. In 2012, a group of Indigenous NRL players including Dean Widders, Preston Campbell, Timana Tahu and George Rose came together to develop a pre-game ceremony that would be a response to New Zealand’s much loved, universally recognised and hugely respected haka. Rather than simply taking an existing dance, the players came up with a series of movements that reflected cultural symbols - the clan, the warrior, the boomerang, the spear. They concluded their new dance with a moment of reflection - to them, this emphasised that the silences are just as important, or even more important, than the spoken words.

programme.title: Pandore

programme.title: Madison

She gives her all to emulate her cool and successful cycle-pro father. But when the talented and ambitious young racer has to unwillingly swap saddles for a mountain bike things go haywire.

programme.title: Down With Love

programme.title: Russian Ark
programme.desc: Told in one fluid real-time shot, this film follows a 19th century French aristocrat - notorious for his scathing memoirs about life in Russia - as he travels through the majestic spaces of the Hermitage in St. Petersburg, engaging real and imagined characters from Russian and European history. Staged among some of Western Art's greatest masterpieces, climaxes in a pageant of colour, motion, and music. The Hermitage - home to generations of Romonovs and the repository of so much Russian history - is the ark of the Russian soul, which he guards affectionately until the world sees better days. Directed by Aleksandr Sokurov, and stars Mariya Kuznetsova and Sergei Dontsov. (From Russia, in Russian, English subtitles) (Drama) (2002) (Rpt) G WS

programme.desc: Eleanor Coppola’s narrative directorial and screenwriting debut stars Academy Award nominee Diane Lane as a Hollywood producer’s wife who unexpectedly takes a trip through France, which reawakens her sense of self and her joie de vivre. Anne (Lane) is at a crossroads in her life. Long married to a successfully driven but inattentive movie producer (Alec Baldwin), she finds herself taking a car trip from Cannes to Paris with a business associate of her husband (Arnaud Viard). What should be a seven-hour drive turns into a journey of discovery involving picturesque sights, fine food and wine, humour, wisdom, and much more.

programme.desc: During a violent storm in the Victorian Highlands, a mother tells her frightened daughter a fable about a great silver brumby who must find its place among its kind, while one man, living in the wilderness, is determined to capture the brumby and tame it. Directed by John Tatoulis and stars Russell Crowe and Caroline Goodall.

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.desc: Centrering her fearless approach to storytelling and her commitment to truth telling through Blak perspectives. Leah sits down with Rachel Perkins to trace a powerful career across stage and screen.

programme.title: Frame By Frame
programme.sub-title: Erica Glynn - My Bed, Your Bed
programme.desc: In this episode Erica Glynn reflects on a career grounded in storytelling, mentorship and cultural authority. Anchored by her short film My Bed, Your Bed.

programme.title: Unmoored
programme.desc: Maria is a successful Swedish TV presenter whose life is turned upside down by shocking accusations made against her husband. To avoid the media attention, they head south on sabbatical. However, an unexpected confrontation triggers a desperate chain of events. Alone, Maria flees to the solitude of the English moors, but her new idyll soon turns to paranoia. As her guilt grows, she is forced to examine the depths of her own self-deception in this psychological suspense drama.

programme.title: Yolngu Boy
programme.desc: About the coming-of-age of three Aboriginal boys in Arnhem Land who inhabit two cultures at once - that of North-East Arnhem Land and also western culture. Botj, Lorrpu and Milika are three Yolngu teenagers who once shared a dream of becoming great hunters. Now aged 14, only Lorrpu hasn't diverged. Botj is a lost soul in trouble with the law, and Milika is more interested in football and girls. One of the central themes of the film is the divide between the prosperity-driven, materialistic western ideal of life and the everyday reality faced by young Aborigines. Directed by Stephen Johnson, and stars Sean Mununggurr and John Sebastian Pilakui.
